children: Wells Fargo said it expects earnings per share growth to start to decelerate.
The market isn't expected to see earnings growth accelerate next year, so Wells Fargo says investors should bet with the few sectors that will - as long as the bond market behaves.

A team at the San Francisco-headquartered bank, led by Ohsung Kwon, chief equity strategist, say it's now at the peak of the EPS cycle, with third-quarter growth coming in at about 32% year-on-year. They see EPS growth starting to slow, with a rate of just over 30% projected for the next two quarters before decelerating to the high-teens by around mid-2027.
"We are moving from 'accelerating profits and positive liquidity' to 'decelerating profits and neutral liquidity,' a decent but not as strong backdrop," the strategists said.

To prepare, Wells Fargo's outlook for the year ahead, published late on Monday, recommends hyperscalers, which it prefers to the receipts of hyperscaler capital expenditure, the semiconductor companies SOX.

The strategists also see health-care companies XLV experiencing continued EPS growth, although warn against extreme bullish sentiment as the bank says the sector has shown some signs of being overbought. Aside from those two industries, the firm expects a broad-based slowdown in S&P 500 earnings, anticipating $425 in 2027, representing growth of 20% year-on-year, and $460 in 2028, marking a rise of just 8%.

The strategists outlined four core risks facing AI in 2027, starting with the need to start justifying multi-billion dollar investments in the tool. For the firm, gross output from AI would likely have to reach $1.4 trillion by 2028 and $2.1 trillion by 2029 to prove satisfactory monetization for investors.

"We believe AI demand will continue to accelerate, but the economy/capital will be the constraint," the team wrote. "We see a risk that the AI capex cycle will enter its late stage in 2027, unless the economy accelerates enough to warrant further investments."

They added that the market is no longer rewarding higher spending on AI alone. Wells Fargo estimates that a third of capex has been financed by debt so far, and now the concentration is on returns on investment.

The strategists equally warn that the AI compute curve is significantly backward-dated, which can be seen in the surging rental price of GPUs. In this case, neoclouds could be in trouble as they pay peak prices for chips.

Finally, the team says the Democrats' victory in the midterm elections could pose risks to the trade. Although the strategists believe concerns over the development of data centers may currently be overstated - particularly because of the economic benefits to local areas - any disruptions at all will only add to current bottlenecks.
The bank also warned of the risk of the yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury BX:TMUBMUSD10Y hovering above 5.25%, describing it as a "tipping point" for equities.
"Historically, that has been the level where the correlation between stocks and rates has been consistently negative, positive only 2% of the time above 5.25%," the strategists said.
The 10-year Treasury on Tuesday, ahead of retail sales data, was yielding 5.10%.
For the S&P 500 SPX, the bank targets 8,200 by the end of 2027, below Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley's forecast of 8,700 and UBS' estimate of 8,900.
